findings.reason: A grep of src finds no AddValidation, IEndpointFilter or validation filter, so the DataAnnotations on SendMailRequest are never checked. ComposeEndpoints.cs:32 dereferences request.To.Length with no null check, and MailSendingService.BuildMimeMessage treats any ContentType other than "html" as plain text.
findings.claim: The validation attributes on SendMailRequest are never enforced. A missing or null To gives a NullReferenceException (500), and the Subject, Body and ContentType limits are not applied.
findings.evidence: The minimal-API handler binds `SendMailRequest request`, and the repo registers no validation filter: grep finds no AddValidation, IEndpointFilter or Validator call in src. So `[Required, MinLength(1)] To`, `[MaxLength(1_048_576)] Body` and `[RegularExpression("^(html|plain)$")] ContentType` are decorative. A JSON body without `to` makes `request.To.Length` throw NullReferenceException at line 32. A null `subject` reaches `message.Subject = request.Subject` in MailSendingService.BuildMimeMessage (line 56), which may throw ArgumentNullException. Any ContentType other than "html" silently becomes plain text. The empty-To case also returns the misleading `InvalidEmailAddress` message.

members.claim: The send endpoint does not enforce its request validation attributes, allowing invalid messages and turning null recipient inputs into server errors.
members.evidence: SendMailRequest declares Required, StringLength, MaxLength and RegularExpression attributes, but Program.cs registers no AddValidation or validation filter. findings.claim: The _isSending guard is set only after async JS interop calls, so a quick double-click can send the email twice.

findings.reason: `client.GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent) ?? ...GetFoldersAsync(...)` only reaches the fallback if GetFolder returns null. MailKit's ImapClient.GetFolder(SpecialFolder) throws NotSupportedException when neither capability is advertised, and the outer catch(Exception) only logs a warning.
findings.claim: GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent) throws on servers without SPECIAL-USE/XLIST, so the fallback lookup by name never runs and the Sent copy is silently skipped.
findings.evidence: `var sent = client.GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent) ?? (await client.GetFoldersAsync(...)).FirstOrDefault(f => f.Name.Equals("Sent", ...));` sits inside a `catch (Exception ex)` that only logs a warning. MailKit's GetFolder(SpecialFolder) throws NotSupportedException when the server does not advertise special-use folders, so the `??` fallback only runs when the capability exists.

findings.reason: markedInterop.toHtml returns marked.parse(markdown) with no sanitiser, and setHtml assigns `this._instance.root.innerHTML = html`, which skips Quill's clipboard path. The input is the user's own composer text, so an attack needs the victim to paste attacker content. I lowered X1's high to medium for that reason.
findings.claim: Switching from Markdown to Rich text puts unsanitised marked output into the page via innerHTML, so raw HTML such as an img onerror handler runs script in the app's origin.
findings.evidence: In Compose.razor, SwitchToRichTextAsync calls `markedInterop.toHtml(_markdownBody)`, and toHtml returns `marked.parse(markdown)` with no sanitizer. setHtml then does `this._instance.root.innerHTML = html;`, which also bypasses Quill's own clipboard/sanitising path. Server-side sanitisation (OutgoingHtmlSanitizer) only covers the outgoing email, not the composer DOM.

findings.reason: SendViaSmtpAsync awaits SendAsync and then DisconnectAsync(quit: true) with no try/catch. An exception during QUIT reaches the endpoint as a 500, and Compose.razor shows ComposeSendFailed and keeps the draft.
findings.claim: If DisconnectAsync throws after SendAsync succeeded, the send is reported as failed, the Sent append is skipped, and a retry by the user delivers the mail twice.
findings.evidence: SendViaSmtpAsync awaits SendAsync and then DisconnectAsync in the same uncaught path. If the server accepts the message but the connection fails during QUIT, the exception propagates through ComposeEndpoints, skipping the Sent append and success response. Compose.SendAsync displays ComposeSendFailed and preserves the draft, allowing the already-delivered message to be resent.

findings.reason: CreateSanitizer clears AllowedSchemes and then adds "data", which HtmlSanitizer applies to all URI attributes. Modern clients block top-level navigation to data: URLs, so the impact is mainly on deliverability. Low.
findings.claim: The outgoing sanitizer allows the data: URI scheme for every URL attribute, including href.
findings.evidence: `sanitizer.AllowedSchemes.Add("data");` applies to all URL attributes, including `href`, not just image sources.
